_help: The Game data page's Quick changes: one entry per row of the card. Each names a table, a row ("*" for every row) or rows, and a column or columns, taken from the game's tables. kind "value" writes the number typed; "factor" writes "xN". negate: the table keeps the number negative and the page shows it positive. chance: no cell may go over 1. names: a row's name in words, for the preview. Every entry is an ordinary cell edit in data.json.
checked: Seen in play: a higher Running speed made the cat run faster. The other numbers load from the same place, but no change to them has been watched in play yet.

rows.label: Running speed
rows.what: How fast your cat runs. Walking is 175. Read by the game's code.

rows.label: Walking speed
rows.what: How fast your cat walks. Running is 390. Read by the game's code.

rows.label: Jump height
rows.what: How high your cat jumps, from standing and from a run alike. Read by the game's code.

rows.label: Stamina used while running
rows.what: How much stamina running uses each second, out of 100. 0 means running never tires your cat. Read by the game's code.

rows.label: Stamina back when resting
rows.what: How much stamina comes back each second while your cat isn't running. Read by the game's code.

rows.label: XP from fights
rows.what: Multiplies the experience every animal gives when you beat it: 2 doubles it. From the tables.

rows.label: Experience each level needs
rows.what: Multiplies the experience each level needs: 0.5 needs half, so levels come twice as fast. From the tables; the notes think each is the experience for that level, not a running total.

rows.label: Inventory space, apprentice
rows.what: How much an apprentice can carry. From the tables.

rows.label: Inventory space, warrior
rows.what: How much a warrior can carry. From the tables.

rows.label: Inventory space, deputy
rows.what: How much a deputy can carry. From the tables.

rows.label: Inventory space, leader
rows.what: How much a leader can carry. From the tables.

rows.label: A mouse is worth
rows.what: How much the fresh-kill pile goes up when you bring a mouse. The pile goes from 0 to 100. From the tables.

rows.label: A bird is worth
rows.what: How much the fresh-kill pile goes up when you bring a bird. From the tables.

rows.label: A squirrel is worth
rows.what: How much the fresh-kill pile goes up when you bring a squirrel. From the tables.

rows.label: A fish is worth
rows.what: How much the fresh-kill pile goes up when you bring a fish. From the tables.

rows.label: A rat is worth
rows.what: How much the fresh-kill pile goes up when you bring a rat. From the tables.

rows.label: A rabbit is worth
rows.what: How much the fresh-kill pile goes up when you bring a rabbit. From the tables.

rows.label: How slowly the pile goes down
rows.what: How long the pile takes to go down by one. At 90 a full pile lasts 2.5 hours of play; higher lasts longer. From the tables.

rows.label: Decoration build time
rows.what: Multiplies how long a den decoration takes to build: 0 makes every one instant. The table gives uncommon ones 4800, rare 14400 and mythic 57600, most likely seconds; whether that's real time isn't checked. From the tables.

rows.label: Kits' size
rows.what: Makes kits bigger or smaller: 1.2 is a fifth bigger. For cats the game makes from now on (a new game's Clans, new kits); cats already in your save keep theirs. From the tables.

rows.label: Apprentices' size
rows.what: Makes apprentices bigger or smaller. For cats the game makes from now on; cats already in your save keep theirs. From the tables.

rows.label: Warriors' size
rows.what: Makes warriors bigger or smaller. For cats the game makes from now on; cats already in your save keep theirs. From the tables.

rows.label: Elders' size
rows.what: Makes elders bigger or smaller. For cats the game makes from now on; cats already in your save keep theirs. From the tables.

rows.label: Leaders' size
rows.what: Makes leaders bigger or smaller. For cats the game makes from now on; cats already in your save keep theirs. From the tables.

rows.label: Warriors' scars
rows.what: Makes scars on warriors more or less likely: 0 means none. A chance can't go over 1. For cats the game makes from now on; cats already in your save keep theirs. From the tables.

rows.label: Deputies' scars
rows.what: Makes scars on deputies more or less likely: 0 means none. For cats the game makes from now on; cats already in your save keep theirs. From the tables.

rows.label: Leaders' scars
rows.what: Makes scars on leaders more or less likely: 0 means none. For cats the game makes from now on; cats already in your save keep theirs. From the tables.

rows.label: Elders' scars
rows.what: Makes scars on elders more or less likely: 0 means none. For cats the game makes from now on; cats already in your save keep theirs. From the tables.

rows.label: Rogues' scars
rows.what: Makes scars on rogues more or less likely: 0 means none. For cats the game makes from now on; cats already in your save keep theirs. From the tables.

rows.label: Two different eyes
rows.what: How often a new cat gets two different eyes: 0.15 is 15 in 100. For cats the game makes from now on. From the tables.

rows.label: The day's clock speed
rows.what: Higher is faster. If it's game seconds for each real second, 72 makes a whole day 20 minutes long; that reading isn't checked. From the tables.
